# Python Cookbook for Brazilian PII

> An open book, in English, about finding and handling Brazilian personal identifiers in text, written for
> engineers whose PII tooling does not know what a CPF is. Eight chapters of code that actually runs: the
> output printed on each page is produced when the book is built, not pasted by hand. Text under CC BY 4.0,
> code under Apache 2.0.

The instrument used throughout is tarja (`pip install tarja`), an Apache 2.0 library with no runtime
dependency, which detects 17 Brazilian identifier types using check digits and Portuguese context words.

Why this exists: Microsoft Presidio ships no Brazilian recognizer at all, and the commercial DLP services
cover only CPF, CNPJ and RG. None of them covers CNS (the health card), CNJ case numbers, voter ID, driving
licence, RENAVAM, or the alphanumeric CNPJ that Brazil began issuing in July 2026.

Five situations this book is for:

- before text reaches a language model, for RAG, search or summarising over your own archive
- as a gate on files leaving your systems, towards a vendor, an email attachment or a public bucket
- to measure exposure across an archive, answering how many documents carry a CPF, which kinds, and where
- before handing data to someone who does not need it, an analyst, a vendor, a staging environment
- to check another tool's work, with a second pass over text somebody already called anonymised

Two things to know before quoting any number from here:

- **Redacting, pseudonymising and anonymising are different, and only the third takes data out of the reach
  of the LGPD.** This book does not teach anonymisation in the sense of art. 12. Chapter 4 explains why, and
  chapter 7 is entirely about the limits.
- **A failing check digit does not mean the value is not personal data.** It is usually a typo or an OCR
  error in a real identifier, and measured, a CPF with one corrupted digit reconstructs to exactly one valid
  CPF in about 93% of cases.

## Chapters

- [1. Your PII tool returns nothing](https://macmaia.github.io/Python-Cookbook-for-Brazilian-PII/01-your-pii-tool-returns-nothing.html): why Presidio finds no CPF out of the box
- [2. Check digits](https://macmaia.github.io/Python-Cookbook-for-Brazilian-PII/02-check-digits.html): the CPF rule written by hand before trusting a library
- [3. When there is no check digit](https://macmaia.github.io/Python-Cookbook-for-Brazilian-PII/03-when-there-is-no-check-digit.html): format-only identifiers and the required context word
- [4. Redact, pseudonymise, anonymise](https://macmaia.github.io/Python-Cookbook-for-Brazilian-PII/04-redact-pseudonymise-anonymise.html): what each choice allows and forbids afterwards
- [5. Before the text reaches an LLM](https://macmaia.github.io/Python-Cookbook-for-Brazilian-PII/05-before-the-text-reaches-an-llm.html): stripping identifiers without breaking retrieval
- [6. Measuring your own error rate](https://macmaia.github.io/Python-Cookbook-for-Brazilian-PII/06-measuring-your-own-error-rate.html): precision and recall on your own data, in both directions
- [7. What none of this does](https://macmaia.github.io/Python-Cookbook-for-Brazilian-PII/07-what-none-of-this-does.html): names, addresses and clinical facts in prose, and the declared limits
- [8. Before you index](https://macmaia.github.io/Python-Cookbook-for-Brazilian-PII/08-before-you-index.html): the RAG corpus, and the identifier split across two chunks
